stages.request: When I save the shopping list with `recipebox shop PLAN --csv FILE`, I'd like every row to say which aisle the item is in, so I can sort and filter the file in a spreadsheet. Please add an `aisle` column as the second column, holding the aisle code such as `produce` or `dairy`, so the header becomes `item,aisle,quantity,unit`.

quiet.path: The CSV module says its file is also for `pantry restock`, and the reference says restock reads a list saved with `shop --csv`; following that leads to `read_purchases`, which unpacks each row by position as item, amount, unit.

stages.request: Thirds come out wrong. A recipe that calls for 1/3 cup of sugar shows `3/8 cup sugar` in `recipebox show`, and showing a 3-serving porridge made with 1 cup of oats at `--servings 1` gives `3/8 cup oats` as well. Amounts should be shown as halves, thirds, quarters or eighths, that is with the denominators `2, 3, 4, 8`, so both of those read `1/3 cup`.

I'm tracking fibre for a diet and chart it from `nutrition_for()`. Please add dietary fibre to the per-serving values it returns, under the key `fibre_g`, right after `carbs_g`, in grams to one decimal like the other gram values, so the fields are `kcal, protein_g, fat_g, carbs_g, fibre_g`. The fibre figures are already in the food composition table.

quiet.path: Following where the per-serving dict goes leads to `render_nutrition`, which looks every key up in its own `LABELS` registry, so a new key needs a label there.

stages.request: Recipe ids are awkward to type on the command line when a title has punctuation or accents: `recipebox add` gives `Mac & Cheese` the id `mac-&-cheese`, which the shell trips over, and `Crème Brûlée!` gets `crème-brûlée!`. Ids should use only the characters `a-z 0-9 -`: drop accents (`é` becomes `e`), treat any other character as a break between words, and join the words with single dashes, with none at the start or end. So `Mac & Cheese` becomes `mac-cheese` and `Crème Brûlée!` becomes `creme-brulee`.

quiet.path: Asking where titles are turned into ids finds `_title_key` in the plan reader, a commented copy of the old id rule that plan files use to find their recipes in the library.

stages.request: Now that the shopping CSV has an aisle column we sort it in the spreadsheet ourselves, and the aisle-first order only makes it harder to find an item. Please have `build_shopping_list()` return its lines in plain alphabetical order of item name (`name`), which also puts the rows of `recipebox shop --csv` in that order.

quiet.path: Following the shopping lines to the printed list finds `render_shopping_list`, whose docstring says its lines come grouped by aisle and which runs `groupby` on them, relying on the aisle order the service used to provide.

stages.request: Our shop keeps eggs in an aisle of their own, away from the dairy. Please add an `eggs` aisle straight after `dairy` and put eggs in it, so the aisle codes in walking order are `produce, bakery, dairy, eggs, meat, pantry, frozen, other`. Eggs should then carry the aisle `eggs` in the lines from `build_shopping_list()` and in the `aisle` column of `recipebox shop --csv`.

quiet.path: Searching for the existing aisle codes (`dairy`) or following the `aisle` field to the printed list finds the `HEADINGS` registry, which gives each aisle code its heading and its place in the walk.

stages.request: `recipebox search` stops at 10 matches by default, which is too few for a broad word like `soup` in our library. Please make the default for `--limit` `25`, and let `--limit 0` mean no limit, printing every match. A negative limit should be refused with the message `--limit must be 0 or more`.

Scripts that read our `library.json` have to parse ingredient amounts such as `"1 1/2"` themselves. Please save each ingredient's `amount` in `library.json` as a JSON `number` (`1.5`) instead of a `string`, keeping `null` for an ingredient without an amount. Libraries saved before this change still have to open. The file keeps `version` 1.

quiet.path: Export bundles are written with `recipe_to_dict`, so the new numbers reach bundles too; the bundle module and the reference say so, and the importer that reads bundles checks that every amount is text.
